slides.say: Without keys, React compares children one by one, in order.
Add an item at the end? Cheap. Add one at the start? React thinks every item changed, and mutates all of them.
With keys, React matches children across renders. It knows 2014 is new, and 2015 and 2016 just moved.

slides.text: Index keys: reorders are slow and state can get mixed up. Random keys recreate everything.
slides.say: Index keys make reorders slow and can mix up component state. Unstable keys, like Math random, recreate nodes and lose state.
